docs.title: Java Common Error Workflow
docs.description: Diagnose recurring Java failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error.
docs.text: Java Common Error Workflow Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Diagnose recurring Java failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error. Why Error text is a symptom, not a root cause. This workflow requires a discriminating observation before each repair. How 1. Preserve timestamps, correlation identifiers, artifact version, topology, and recent changes. 2. Stabilize user impact with the smallest reversible mitigation. 3. Capture the evidence named below before restarting or clearing state. 4. Test one ranked hypothesis at a time. 5. Add a regression test, alert, or policy after confirming root cause. Symptom Likely causal class Required repair Primary evidence --- --- --- --- BeanCurrentlyInCreationException Spring beans form a circular dependency. Refactor shared behavior behind a lower-level port; do not enable circular references. Spring condition report LazyInitializationException A lazy association is accessed after its persistence context closes. Fetch the use-case projection inside the transaction. Hibernate SQL logs TransactionRequiredException A write runs outside an active transaction. Place the transaction on the public use-case method. transaction trace logging Connection pool timeout Transactions are slow, leaked, or pool sizing mismatches load. Measure hold time, close resources, and bound concurrency. JFR and pool metrics OutOfMemoryError Heap, metaspace, direct memory, or native resources are exhausted. Capture the correct dump and fix retention before changing limits. JFR and heap dump 1. BeanCurrentlyInCreationException Confirm: Capture Spring condition report and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Spring beans form a circular dependency. Repair: Refactor shared behavior behind a lower-level port; do not enable circular references. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 2. LazyInitializationException Confirm: Capture Hibernate SQL logs and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: A lazy association is accessed after its persistence context closes. Repair: Fetch the use-case projection inside the transaction. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 3. TransactionRequiredException Confirm: Capture transaction trace logging and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: A write runs outside an active transaction. Repair: Place the transaction on the public use-case method. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 4. Connection pool timeout Confirm: Capture JFR and pool metrics and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Transactions are slow, leaked, or pool sizing mismatches load. Repair: Measure hold time, close resources, and bound concurrency. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 5. OutOfMemoryError Confirm: Capture JFR and heap dump and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Heap, metaspace, direct memory, or native resources are exhausted. Repair: Capture the correct dump and fix retention before changing limits. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated diagnostic or repair without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - Java documentation - Spring Boot reference - Spring transaction management Checklist - [ ] Incident timeline and affected artifact identity are preserved. - [ ] Root cause explains every material observation. - [ ] Mitigation is reversible and does not destroy forensic state. - [ ] Permanent fix has a regression test. - [ ] Recovery is confirmed through user-impact telemetry. docs.title: Kubernetes Common Error Workflow
docs.description: Diagnose recurring Kubernetes failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error.
docs.text: Kubernetes Common Error Workflow Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Diagnose recurring Kubernetes failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error. Why Error text is a symptom, not a root cause. This workflow requires a discriminating observation before each repair. How 1. Preserve timestamps, correlation identifiers, artifact version, topology, and recent changes. 2. Stabilize user impact with the smallest reversible mitigation. 3. Capture the evidence named below before restarting or clearing state. 4. Test one ranked hypothesis at a time. 5. Add a regression test, alert, or policy after confirming root cause. Symptom Likely causal class Required repair Primary evidence --- --- --- --- CrashLoopBackOff The container repeatedly exits or fails startup probes. Inspect previous logs, termination reason, config, and startup dependencies. kubectl describe and logs --previous ImagePullBackOff Image name, tag/digest, registry access, or credentials are invalid. Verify digest and node-side registry authentication. Pod events Pending Pod Scheduler cannot satisfy resources, affinity, taints, or volume constraints. Read scheduling events and correct the specific unsatisfied predicate. kubectl describe pod OOMKilled Container exceeds its memory limit or node experiences pressure. Profile working set and leaks; set evidence-based requests and limits. container metrics Service unreachable Selector, endpoints, port mapping, policy, or DNS is wrong. Trace DNS to Service to EndpointSlice to Pod from the caller. EndpointSlice and ephemeral debug container 1. CrashLoopBackOff Confirm: Capture kubectl describe and logs --previous and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: The container repeatedly exits or fails startup probes. Repair: Inspect previous logs, termination reason, config, and startup dependencies. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 2. ImagePullBackOff Confirm: Capture Pod events and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Image name, tag/digest, registry access, or credentials are invalid. Repair: Verify digest and node-side registry authentication. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 3. Pending Pod Confirm: Capture kubectl describe pod and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Scheduler cannot satisfy resources, affinity, taints, or volume constraints. Repair: Read scheduling events and correct the specific unsatisfied predicate. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 4. OOMKilled Confirm: Capture container metrics and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Container exceeds its memory limit or node experiences pressure. Repair: Profile working set and leaks; set evidence-based requests and limits. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 5. Service unreachable Confirm: Capture EndpointSlice and ephemeral debug container and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Selector, endpoints, port mapping, policy, or DNS is wrong. Repair: Trace DNS to Service to EndpointSlice to Pod from the caller. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated diagnostic or repair without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - Kubernetes documentation - Debug applications - Security checklist Checklist - [ ] Incident timeline and affected artifact identity are preserved. - [ ] Root cause explains every material observation. - [ ] Mitigation is reversible and does not destroy forensic state. - [ ] Permanent fix has a regression test. - [ ] Recovery is confirmed through user-impact telemetry. docs.text: Kubernetes Production Skill Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Provide a deterministic procedure for generating, changing, diagnosing, or releasing a Kubernetes workload, controller manifest, Helm/Kustomize release, or runbook with AI assistance. Trigger Activate when a request changes Kubernetes source, configuration, infrastructure, data contracts, or production behavior. Do not activate for a documentation-only mention with no technical decision. Why Deploy through controllers, declare resource and health contracts, use least-privilege identities, and diagnose from events before logs. The skill converts that principle into evidence gates that an agent cannot skip. Inputs - Repository rules and ownership boundaries. - Exact runtime/toolchain evidence from manifests or platform APIs. - Requested behavior and acceptance tests. - Sanitized logs, traces, metrics, plans, or screenshots when diagnosing. - Deployment topology, SLO, data classification, and rollback mechanism. How 1. Discover the nearest repository instructions and established implementation pattern. 2. State the invariant, trust boundary, failure mode, and rollback boundary. 3. Select the matching prompt under ../prompts/. 4. Make the smallest coherent change; preserve public contracts unless migration is approved. 5. Run native formatting, static analysis, unit/integration tests, security checks, and build/package validation. 6. Apply ../checklists/code-review.md. 7. For release work, apply ../checklists/deployment.md and capture evidence. Verification 1. Verify that requests and limits reflect measurements. 2. Verify that startup/readiness/liveness semantics differ correctly. 3. Verify that RBAC and network policy are least privilege. 4. Verify that rollout and rollback are verified. 5. Record commands, exit status, artifact identity, and links to retained evidence. Unhappy path and recovery - If repository or version evidence is missing, stop and request it. - If a validator fails, fix the first causal error; never suppress the rule as the initial response. - If the failure cannot be reproduced, improve telemetry and preserve the incident state. - If a release gate fails, halt progression and execute the documented rollback or feature-disable path. - If credentials or regulated data appear in context, stop, revoke or rotate as required, and follow incident policy. Communication protocol Report decisions, changed files, commands actually run, observed results, residual risks, and an explicit ship/block recommendation. Distinguish facts from hypotheses. Termination criteria Finish only when acceptance tests and both relevant checklists pass, or when a named blocker with owner and required evidence is recorded. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated Kubernetes workload, controller manifest, Helm/Kustomize release, or runbook without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - Kubernetes documentation - Debug applications - Security checklist Checklist - [ ] Trigger and scope are valid. - [ ] Inputs are complete and sanitized. - [ ] Native validators pass. - [ ] Failure and rollback paths are tested. - [ ] Evidence is retained under project policy. docs.text: Microfrontends Architecture Patterns Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Define the default production architecture for a Microfrontends workload and the boundaries an AI-generated change must preserve. Why Split only by durable business domains, keep one shell contract, isolate failures, and prove independent deployment before accepting runtime federation. A stable boundary reduces coupling, limits failure propagation, and makes ownership auditable. How Use Domain slice behind shell: The shell owns navigation, identity context, and failure boundaries; each domain independently builds immutable assets. Boundary rules 1. Validate identity, authorization, and input before domain mutation. 2. Keep dependency-specific types behind the infrastructure port. 3. Attach deadlines, cancellation, idempotency, and retry classification at the call boundary. 4. Emit traceable outcomes without secret or regulated payload leakage. 5. Version contracts and migrate producers before removing compatibility. Tradeoffs The extra adapter and contract code costs initial delivery time. It buys isolated tests, replaceable infrastructure, clearer ownership, and safer migrations. Anti-patterns - Split by UI widgets or engineering teams without domain boundaries. This couples unrelated change rates and expands blast radius. - Do not hide remote calls, unbounded work, or mutable global state behind convenience helpers. - Do not introduce a distributed boundary without an owner, SLO, timeout, and failure policy. Enterprise considerations Assign owners to every boundary and data class. Enforce policy as code, retain architecture decisions and deployment evidence, and design regional, tenant, and regulatory isolation before data is written. Official guidance - Micro Frontends architecture article - webpack Module Federation - W3C Custom Elements Checklist - [ ] Domain and infrastructure boundaries are visible in code and telemetry. - [ ] Trust, data, transaction, and rollback boundaries are documented. - [ ] Dependency failure is bounded and tested. - [ ] Contract evolution is backward compatible. - [ ] Ownership and SLO are assigned. docs.text: Microfrontends Production Skill Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Provide a deterministic procedure for generating, changing, diagnosing, or releasing a frontend slice, shell contract, federated module, routing boundary, or release runbook with AI assistance. Trigger Activate when a request changes Microfrontends source, configuration, infrastructure, data contracts, or production behavior. Do not activate for a documentation-only mention with no technical decision. Why Split only by durable business domains, keep one shell contract, isolate failures, and prove independent deployment before accepting runtime federation. The skill converts that principle into evidence gates that an agent cannot skip. Inputs - Repository rules and ownership boundaries. - Exact runtime/toolchain evidence from manifests or platform APIs. - Requested behavior and acceptance tests. - Sanitized logs, traces, metrics, plans, or screenshots when diagnosing. - Deployment topology, SLO, data classification, and rollback mechanism. How 1. Discover the nearest repository instructions and established implementation pattern. 2. State the invariant, trust boundary, failure mode, and rollback boundary. 3. Select the matching prompt under ../prompts/. 4. Make the smallest coherent change; preserve public contracts unless migration is approved. 5. Run native formatting, static analysis, unit/integration tests, security checks, and build/package validation. 6. Apply ../checklists/code-review.md. 7. For release work, apply ../checklists/deployment.md and capture evidence. Verification 1. Verify that ownership aligns to business domain. 2. Verify that shell contracts are versioned. 3. Verify that shared dependencies have one policy. 4. Verify that slice failure degrades locally. 5. Record commands, exit status, artifact identity, and links to retained evidence. docs.title: MongoDB Architecture Patterns
docs.description: Define the default production architecture for a MongoDB workload and the boundaries an AI-generated change must preserve.
docs.text: MongoDB Architecture Patterns Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Define the default production architecture for a MongoDB workload and the boundaries an AI-generated change must preserve. Why Model documents around atomic access patterns, enforce schema validation, and design shard and index keys from measured queries. A stable boundary reduces coupling, limits failure propagation, and makes ownership auditable. How Use Aggregate document boundary: Embed data read and updated together within bounded growth; reference independent or unbounded aggregates. Boundary rules 1. Validate identity, authorization, and input before domain mutation. 2. Keep dependency-specific types behind the infrastructure port. 3. Attach deadlines, cancellation, idempotency, and retry classification at the call boundary. 4. Emit traceable outcomes without secret or regulated payload leakage. 5. Version contracts and migrate producers before removing compatibility. Tradeoffs The extra adapter and contract code costs initial delivery time. It buys isolated tests, replaceable infrastructure, clearer ownership, and safer migrations. Anti-patterns - Normalize every relationship as if MongoDB were relational. This couples unrelated change rates and expands blast radius. - Do not hide remote calls, unbounded work, or mutable global state behind convenience helpers. - Do not introduce a distributed boundary without an owner, SLO, timeout, and failure policy. Enterprise considerations Assign owners to every boundary and data class. Enforce policy as code, retain architecture decisions and deployment evidence, and design regional, tenant, and regulatory isolation before data is written. Official guidance - MongoDB documentation - Data modeling - Query plans Checklist - [ ] Domain and infrastructure boundaries are visible in code and telemetry. - [ ] Trust, data, transaction, and rollback boundaries are documented. - [ ] Dependency failure is bounded and tested. - [ ] Contract evolution is backward compatible. - [ ] Ownership and SLO are assigned. docs.title: MongoDB Common Error Workflow
docs.description: Diagnose recurring MongoDB failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error.
docs.text: MongoDB Common Error Workflow Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Diagnose recurring MongoDB failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error. Why Error text is a symptom, not a root cause. This workflow requires a discriminating observation before each repair. How 1. Preserve timestamps, correlation identifiers, artifact version, topology, and recent changes. 2. Stabilize user impact with the smallest reversible mitigation. 3. Capture the evidence named below before restarting or clearing state. 4. Test one ranked hypothesis at a time. 5. Add a regression test, alert, or policy after confirming root cause. Symptom Likely causal class Required repair Primary evidence --- --- --- --- E11000 duplicate key A write violates a unique index or races with another writer. Treat the index as the authority and implement idempotent conflict handling. index metadata Exceeded memory limit for aggregation A stage requires unbounded in-memory state. Filter early, use supporting indexes, bound groups/sorts, and assess disk use. explain executionStats Transaction numbers are only allowed on a replica set Transactions are attempted on unsupported standalone topology. Use a replica set or redesign around document-level atomicity. hello command Shard key update or routing failure Write lacks the required key or targets an immutable/routing constraint. Include the full routing key and redesign key changes as controlled moves. sharding metadata Server selection timeout Driver cannot discover a healthy compatible server. Check URI, DNS, TLS, firewall, topology, and driver diagnostics. driver topology logs 1. E11000 duplicate key Confirm: Capture index metadata and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: A write violates a unique index or races with another writer. Repair: Treat the index as the authority and implement idempotent conflict handling. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 2. Exceeded memory limit for aggregation Confirm: Capture explain executionStats and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: A stage requires unbounded in-memory state. Repair: Filter early, use supporting indexes, bound groups/sorts, and assess disk use. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 3. Transaction numbers are only allowed on a replica set Confirm: Capture hello command and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Transactions are attempted on unsupported standalone topology. Repair: Use a replica set or redesign around document-level atomicity. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 4. Shard key update or routing failure Confirm: Capture sharding metadata and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Write lacks the required key or targets an immutable/routing constraint. Repair: Include the full routing key and redesign key changes as controlled moves. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 5. Server selection timeout Confirm: Capture driver topology logs and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Driver cannot discover a healthy compatible server. Repair: Check URI, DNS, TLS, firewall, topology, and driver diagnostics. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated diagnostic or repair without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - MongoDB documentation - Data modeling - Query plans Checklist - [ ] Incident timeline and affected artifact identity are preserved. - [ ] Root cause explains every material observation. - [ ] Mitigation is reversible and does not destroy forensic state. - [ ] Permanent fix has a regression test. - [ ] Recovery is confirmed through user-impact telemetry. docs.description: Define the default production architecture for a Next.js workload and the boundaries an AI-generated change must preserve.
docs.text: Next.js Architecture Patterns Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Define the default production architecture for a Next.js workload and the boundaries an AI-generated change must preserve. Why Default to Server Components; add client boundaries only for browser APIs or interactivity, and make cache behavior explicit. A stable boundary reduces coupling, limits failure propagation, and makes ownership auditable. How Use Server-first route slice: Layouts compose server-rendered feature slices; client islands contain only interactive state. Boundary rules 1. Validate identity, authorization, and input before domain mutation. 2. Keep dependency-specific types behind the infrastructure port. 3. Attach deadlines, cancellation, idempotency, and retry classification at the call boundary. 4. Emit traceable outcomes without secret or regulated payload leakage. 5. Version contracts and migrate producers before removing compatibility. Tradeoffs The extra adapter and contract code costs initial delivery time. It buys isolated tests, replaceable infrastructure, clearer ownership, and safer migrations. Anti-patterns - Mark whole pages use client. This couples unrelated change rates and expands blast radius. - Do not hide remote calls, unbounded work, or mutable global state behind convenience helpers. - Do not introduce a distributed boundary without an owner, SLO, timeout, and failure policy. Enterprise considerations Assign owners to every boundary and data class. Enforce policy as code, retain architecture decisions and deployment evidence, and design regional, tenant, and regulatory isolation before data is written. Official guidance - Next.js App Router - Server and Client Components - Caching Checklist - [ ] Domain and infrastructure boundaries are visible in code and telemetry. - [ ] Trust, data, transaction, and rollback boundaries are documented. - [ ] Dependency failure is bounded and tested. - [ ] Contract evolution is backward compatible. - [ ] Ownership and SLO are assigned. docs.text: Next.js Code Review Checklist Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Review a Next.js change for correctness, security, operability, and maintainability before merge. Why Checklists convert production expectations into auditable yes/no gates and prevent AI-generated plausibility from replacing runtime evidence. How Review the diff with repository context, then execute validators. Record only evidence-backed findings with a required fix and verification method. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated route, layout, Server Component, or Route Handler without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - Next.js App Router - Server and Client Components - Caching Checklist - [ ] Change follows the governing stance: Default to Server Components; add client boundaries only for browser APIs or interactivity, and make cache behavior explicit. - [ ] Public behavior and compatibility impact are documented. - [ ] Input validation, authorization, output encoding, and secret handling match the threat model. - [ ] Failure paths define timeout, cancellation, retry safety, idempotency, and cleanup where applicable. - [ ] Concurrency and transaction behavior preserve data invariants. - [ ] Logs, metrics, and traces identify outcomes without sensitive payloads. - [ ] Tests cover success, boundary, failure, and recovery behavior. - [ ] Native formatter, static analysis, tests, security checks, and build pass. - [ ] Server/client boundaries are minimal. - [ ] Dynamic and cache behavior is explicit. - [ ] Route errors and loading states exist. - [ ] Metadata and canonical URLs are correct. - [ ] Documentation and runbooks match changed behavior. docs.title: Next.js Common Error Workflow
docs.description: Diagnose recurring Next.js failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error.
docs.text: Next.js Common Error Workflow Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Diagnose recurring Next.js failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error. Why Error text is a symptom, not a root cause. This workflow requires a discriminating observation before each repair. How 1. Preserve timestamps, correlation identifiers, artifact version, topology, and recent changes. 2. Stabilize user impact with the smallest reversible mitigation. 3. Capture the evidence named below before restarting or clearing state. 4. Test one ranked hypothesis at a time. 5. Add a regression test, alert, or policy after confirming root cause. Symptom Likely causal class Required repair Primary evidence --- --- --- --- You're importing a component that needs useState A Server Component imports client-only behavior. Move the smallest interactive subtree behind a use client boundary. next build Dynamic server usage A static route reads request-specific data. Declare the route dynamic or move request access into an appropriate dynamic boundary. next build Hydration failed Client output differs from server HTML. Remove time, randomness, or browser-only branches from initial render. browser console Route Handler returns stale data Cache semantics were left implicit. Declare revalidation or no-store behavior at the data boundary. response cache headers NEXTREDIRECT surfaced as an error redirect was caught by a broad catch block. Call redirect outside try/catch or rethrow framework control-flow errors. server logs 1. You're importing a component that needs useState Confirm: Capture next build and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: A Server Component imports client-only behavior. Repair: Move the smallest interactive subtree behind a use client boundary. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 2. Dynamic server usage Confirm: Capture next build and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: A static route reads request-specific data. Repair: Declare the route dynamic or move request access into an appropriate dynamic boundary. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 3. Hydration failed Confirm: Capture browser console and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Client output differs from server HTML. Repair: Remove time, randomness, or browser-only branches from initial render. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 4. Route Handler returns stale data Confirm: Capture response cache headers and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Cache semantics were left implicit. Repair: Declare revalidation or no-store behavior at the data boundary. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 5. NEXTREDIRECT surfaced as an error Confirm: Capture server logs and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: redirect was caught by a broad catch block. Repair: Call redirect outside try/catch or rethrow framework control-flow errors. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated diagnostic or repair without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - Next.js App Router - Server and Client Components - Caching Checklist - [ ] Incident timeline and affected artifact identity are preserved. - [ ] Root cause explains every material observation. - [ ] Mitigation is reversible and does not destroy forensic state. - [ ] Permanent fix has a regression test. - [ ] Recovery is confirmed through user-impact telemetry. docs.text: Next.js Production Skill Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Provide a deterministic procedure for generating, changing, diagnosing, or releasing a route, layout, Server Component, or Route Handler with AI assistance. Trigger Activate when a request changes Next.js source, configuration, infrastructure, data contracts, or production behavior. Do not activate for a documentation-only mention with no technical decision. Why Default to Server Components; add client boundaries only for browser APIs or interactivity, and make cache behavior explicit. The skill converts that principle into evidence gates that an agent cannot skip. Inputs - Repository rules and ownership boundaries. - Exact runtime/toolchain evidence from manifests or platform APIs. - Requested behavior and acceptance tests. - Sanitized logs, traces, metrics, plans, or screenshots when diagnosing. - Deployment topology, SLO, data classification, and rollback mechanism. How 1. Discover the nearest repository instructions and established implementation pattern. 2. State the invariant, trust boundary, failure mode, and rollback boundary. 3. Select the matching prompt under ../prompts/. 4. Make the smallest coherent change; preserve public contracts unless migration is approved. 5. Run native formatting, static analysis, unit/integration tests, security checks, and build/package validation. 6. Apply ../checklists/code-review.md. 7. For release work, apply ../checklists/deployment.md and capture evidence. Verification 1. Verify that server/client boundaries are minimal. 2. Verify that dynamic and cache behavior is explicit. 3. Verify that route errors and loading states exist. 4. Verify that metadata and canonical URLs are correct. 5. Record commands, exit status, artifact identity, and links to retained evidence. Unhappy path and recovery - If repository or version evidence is missing, stop and request it. - If a validator fails, fix the first causal error; never suppress the rule as the initial response. - If the failure cannot be reproduced, improve telemetry and preserve the incident state. - If a release gate fails, halt progression and execute the documented rollback or feature-disable path. - If credentials or regulated data appear in context, stop, revoke or rotate as required, and follow incident policy. Communication protocol Report decisions, changed files, commands actually run, observed results, residual risks, and an explicit ship/block recommendation. Distinguish facts from hypotheses. Termination criteria Finish only when acceptance tests and both relevant checklists pass, or when a named blocker with owner and required evidence is recorded. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated route, layout, Server Component, or Route Handler without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - Next.js App Router - Server and Client Components - Caching Checklist - [ ] Trigger and scope are valid. - [ ] Inputs are complete and sanitized. - [ ] Native validators pass. - [ ] Failure and rollback paths are tested. - [ ] Evidence is retained under project policy. docs.text: Node.js Architecture Patterns Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Define the default production architecture for a Node.js workload and the boundaries an AI-generated change must preserve. Why Keep the event loop non-blocking, propagate cancellation, bound concurrency, and terminate only after draining in-flight work. A stable boundary reduces coupling, limits failure propagation, and makes ownership auditable. How Use Ports-and-adapters service: Transport validates input and calls domain use cases through explicit infrastructure ports. Boundary rules 1. Validate identity, authorization, and input before domain mutation. 2. Keep dependency-specific types behind the infrastructure port. 3. Attach deadlines, cancellation, idempotency, and retry classification at the call boundary. 4. Emit traceable outcomes without secret or regulated payload leakage. 5. Version contracts and migrate producers before removing compatibility. Tradeoffs The extra adapter and contract code costs initial delivery time. It buys isolated tests, replaceable infrastructure, clearer ownership, and safer migrations. Anti-patterns - Put database and HTTP clients directly in route handlers. This couples unrelated change rates and expands blast radius. - Do not hide remote calls, unbounded work, or mutable global state behind convenience helpers. - Do not introduce a distributed boundary without an owner, SLO, timeout, and failure policy. Enterprise considerations Assign owners to every boundary and data class. Enforce policy as code, retain architecture decisions and deployment evidence, and design regional, tenant, and regulatory isolation before data is written. Official guidance - Node.js API documentation - Don't block the event loop - OWASP Node.js guide Checklist - [ ] Domain and infrastructure boundaries are visible in code and telemetry. - [ ] Trust, data, transaction, and rollback boundaries are documented. - [ ] Dependency failure is bounded and tested. - [ ] Contract evolution is backward compatible. - [ ] Ownership and SLO are assigned. docs.text: Node.js Cookbook Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose This cookbook turns Node.js production guidance into reusable prompts, a procedural skill, diagnostics, architecture patterns, and release gates. Why AI output is safe only when constrained by the runtime's real contracts. For Node.js, the decisive concerns are HTTP APIs, asynchronous control flow, streams, process lifecycle, observability, and dependency safety. The governing stance is: Keep the event loop non-blocking, propagate cancellation, bound concurrency, and terminate only after draining in-flight work. When to use Use this cookbook to generate, review, debug, or deploy a service, API handler, worker, or library module. Do not use it as a substitute for repository conventions, threat modeling, load testing, or operator approval. How 1. Start with prompts/generate.prompt.md and supply repository evidence. 2. Run native format, static-analysis, test, security, and build commands. 3. Apply prompts/review.prompt.md; block on unresolved correctness or security findings. 4. Use debug-workflows/common-errors.md from observed evidence, not guesses. 5. Enforce both files under checklists/ before release. Contents - Three production XML prompts: generate, review, and debug. - One trigger-based node.skill.md. - Five evidence-led common-error workflows. - One opinionated architecture pattern. - Separate code-review and deployment gates. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated service, API handler, worker, or library module without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - Node.js API documentation - Don't block the event loop - OWASP Node.js guide Checklist - [ ] Async failures reach one error boundary. - [ ] Timeouts and cancellation propagate. - [ ] Inputs are schema-validated. - [ ] Shutdown drains in-flight work. - [ ] Links in this cookbook resolve to official guidance. - [ ] Prompt output includes no unresolved variables. docs.description: Provide a deterministic procedure for generating, changing, diagnosing, or releasing a service, API handler, worker, or library module with AI assistance.
docs.text: Node.js Production Skill Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Provide a deterministic procedure for generating, changing, diagnosing, or releasing a service, API handler, worker, or library module with AI assistance. Trigger Activate when a request changes Node.js source, configuration, infrastructure, data contracts, or production behavior. Do not activate for a documentation-only mention with no technical decision. Why Keep the event loop non-blocking, propagate cancellation, bound concurrency, and terminate only after draining in-flight work. The skill converts that principle into evidence gates that an agent cannot skip. Inputs - Repository rules and ownership boundaries. - Exact runtime/toolchain evidence from manifests or platform APIs. - Requested behavior and acceptance tests. - Sanitized logs, traces, metrics, plans, or screenshots when diagnosing. - Deployment topology, SLO, data classification, and rollback mechanism. How 1. Discover the nearest repository instructions and established implementation pattern. 2. State the invariant, trust boundary, failure mode, and rollback boundary. 3. Select the matching prompt under ../prompts/. 4. Make the smallest coherent change; preserve public contracts unless migration is approved. 5. Run native formatting, static analysis, unit/integration tests, security checks, and build/package validation. 6. Apply ../checklists/code-review.md. 7. For release work, apply ../checklists/deployment.md and capture evidence. Verification 1. Verify that async failures reach one error boundary. 2. Verify that timeouts and cancellation propagate. 3. Verify that inputs are schema-validated. 4. Verify that shutdown drains in-flight work. 5. Record commands, exit status, artifact identity, and links to retained evidence. Unhappy path and recovery - If repository or version evidence is missing, stop and request it. - If a validator fails, fix the first causal error; never suppress the rule as the initial response. - If the failure cannot be reproduced, improve telemetry and preserve the incident state. - If a release gate fails, halt progression and execute the documented rollback or feature-disable path. - If credentials or regulated data appear in context, stop, revoke or rotate as required, and follow incident policy. Communication protocol Report decisions, changed files, commands actually run, observed results, residual risks, and an explicit ship/block recommendation. Distinguish facts from hypotheses. Termination criteria Finish only when acceptance tests and both relevant checklists pass, or when a named blocker with owner and required evidence is recorded. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated service, API handler, worker, or library module without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - Node.js API documentation - Don't block the event loop - OWASP Node.js guide Checklist - [ ] Trigger and scope are valid. - [ ] Inputs are complete and sanitized. - [ ] Native validators pass. - [ ] Failure and rollback paths are tested. - [ ] Evidence is retained under project policy. docs.title: Performance Engineering Architecture Patterns
docs.description: Define the default production architecture for a Performance Engineering workload and the boundaries an AI-generated change must preserve.
docs.text: Performance Engineering Architecture Patterns Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Define the default production architecture for a Performance Engineering workload and the boundaries an AI-generated change must preserve. Why Optimize only against a reproducible workload and user-impact metric; enforce budgets in CI and confirm gains in production telemetry. A stable boundary reduces coupling, limits failure propagation, and makes ownership auditable. How Use Budget-driven feedback loop: SLOs define budgets; RUM and service telemetry detect impact; CI catches reproducible regressions. Boundary rules 1. Validate identity, authorization, and input before domain mutation. 2. Keep dependency-specific types behind the infrastructure port. 3. Attach deadlines, cancellation, idempotency, and retry classification at the call boundary. 4. Emit traceable outcomes without secret or regulated payload leakage. 5. Version contracts and migrate producers before removing compatibility. Tradeoffs The extra adapter and contract code costs initial delivery time. It buys isolated tests, replaceable infrastructure, clearer ownership, and safer migrations. Anti-patterns - Optimize code based on intuition or one local run. This couples unrelated change rates and expands blast radius. - Do not hide remote calls, unbounded work, or mutable global state behind convenience helpers. - Do not introduce a distributed boundary without an owner, SLO, timeout, and failure policy. Enterprise considerations Assign owners to every boundary and data class. Enforce policy as code, retain architecture decisions and deployment evidence, and design regional, tenant, and regulatory isolation before data is written. Official guidance - Web Vitals - OpenTelemetry performance - Google SRE monitoring Checklist - [ ] Domain and infrastructure boundaries are visible in code and telemetry. - [ ] Trust, data, transaction, and rollback boundaries are documented. - [ ] Dependency failure is bounded and tested. - [ ] Contract evolution is backward compatible. - [ ] Ownership and SLO are assigned. docs.title: Performance Engineering Common Error Workflow
docs.description: Diagnose recurring Performance Engineering failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error.
docs.text: Performance Engineering Common Error Workflow Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Diagnose recurring Performance Engineering failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error. Why Error text is a symptom, not a root cause. This workflow requires a discriminating observation before each repair. How 1. Preserve timestamps, correlation identifiers, artifact version, topology, and recent changes. 2. Stabilize user impact with the smallest reversible mitigation. 3. Capture the evidence named below before restarting or clearing state. 4. Test one ranked hypothesis at a time. 5. Add a regression test, alert, or policy after confirming root cause. Symptom Likely causal class Required repair Primary evidence --- --- --- --- High p99 with normal average A tail cohort, queue, retry, or dependency dominates rare requests. Segment traces by route, dependency, region, and payload; remove the tail cause. distributed traces and histograms Benchmark improves but production does not Synthetic workload omits the production bottleneck or cache state. Rebuild the workload from production distributions and validate with telemetry. profile comparison CPU saturation Concurrency exceeds compute capacity or hot code consumes excessive cycles. Profile on representative load, optimize the hot path, then cap concurrency. sampling profiler Memory growth Objects, caches, listeners, or native allocations are retained. Compare heap snapshots by retaining path and bound cache ownership. heap profiler Core Web Vital regression A release changed critical rendering, interaction, or layout behavior. Use field data to isolate template/device cohorts, then reproduce in lab. CrUX/RUM and browser trace 1. High p99 with normal average Confirm: Capture distributed traces and histograms and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: A tail cohort, queue, retry, or dependency dominates rare requests. Repair: Segment traces by route, dependency, region, and payload; remove the tail cause. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 2. Benchmark improves but production does not Confirm: Capture profile comparison and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Synthetic workload omits the production bottleneck or cache state. Repair: Rebuild the workload from production distributions and validate with telemetry. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 3. CPU saturation Confirm: Capture sampling profiler and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Concurrency exceeds compute capacity or hot code consumes excessive cycles. Repair: Profile on representative load, optimize the hot path, then cap concurrency. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 4. Memory growth Confirm: Capture heap profiler and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Objects, caches, listeners, or native allocations are retained. Repair: Compare heap snapshots by retaining path and bound cache ownership. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 5. Core Web Vital regression Confirm: Capture CrUX/RUM and browser trace and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: A release changed critical rendering, interaction, or layout behavior. Repair: Use field data to isolate template/device cohorts, then reproduce in lab. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated diagnostic or repair without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - Web Vitals - OpenTelemetry performance - Google SRE monitoring Checklist - [ ] Incident timeline and affected artifact identity are preserved. - [ ] Root cause explains every material observation. - [ ] Mitigation is reversible and does not destroy forensic state. - [ ] Permanent fix has a regression test. - [ ] Recovery is confirmed through user-impact telemetry. Changelog - 1.0.0 (2026-07-16): Added production five-error diagnostic workflow.

docs.text: PostgreSQL Architecture Patterns Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Define the default production architecture for a PostgreSQL workload and the boundaries an AI-generated change must preserve. Attach deadlines, cancellation, idempotency, and retry classification at the call boundary. 4. Emit traceable outcomes without secret or regulated payload leakage. 5. Enforce policy as code, retain architecture decisions and deployment evidence, and design regional, tenant, and regulatory isolation before data is written. docs.text: PostgreSQL Common Error Workflow Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Diagnose recurring PostgreSQL failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error. Why Error text is a symptom, not a root cause. This workflow requires a discriminating observation before each repair. How 1. Preserve timestamps, correlation identifiers, artifact version, topology, and recent changes. 2. Stabilize user impact with the smallest reversible mitigation. 3. Capture the evidence named below before restarting or clearing state. 4. Test one ranked hypothesis at a time. 5. Add a regression test, alert, or policy after confirming root cause. Symptom Likely causal class Required repair Primary evidence --- --- --- --- deadlock detected Transactions lock the same resources in inconsistent order. Standardize lock order, shorten transactions, and retry the whole transaction. loglockwaits and pgstatactivity remaining connection slots are reserved Clients exceed connection capacity or leak sessions. Use bounded pools, find leaks, and reserve operator access. pgstatactivity canceling statement due to statement timeout Query plan or lock wait exceeds its budget. Separate execution from lock time, inspect blockers and actual plan. pgstatactivity and EXPLAIN duplicate key violates unique constraint Concurrency or idempotency violates a declared uniqueness invariant. Use an atomic upsert or return the existing idempotent result. constraint metadata replica lag Replay cannot keep up because of write volume, I/O, conflicts, or long queries. Measure WAL generation/replay and remove the limiting cause. pgstatreplication 1. deadlock detected Confirm: Capture loglockwaits and pgstatactivity and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Transactions lock the same resources in inconsistent order. Repair: Standardize lock order, shorten transactions, and retry the whole transaction. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 2. remaining connection slots are reserved Confirm: Capture pgstatactivity and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Clients exceed connection capacity or leak sessions. Repair: Use bounded pools, find leaks, and reserve operator access. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 3. canceling statement due to statement timeout Confirm: Capture pgstatactivity and EXPLAIN and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Query plan or lock wait exceeds its budget. Repair: Separate execution from lock time, inspect blockers and actual plan. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 4. duplicate key violates unique constraint Confirm: Capture constraint metadata and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Concurrency or idempotency violates a declared uniqueness invariant. Repair: Use an atomic upsert or return the existing idempotent result. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 5. replica lag Confirm: Capture pgstatreplication and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Replay cannot keep up because of write volume, I/O, conflicts, or long queries. Repair: Measure WAL generation/replay and remove the limiting cause. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated diagnostic or repair without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - PostgreSQL documentation - EXPLAIN - Explicit locking Checklist - [ ] Incident timeline and affected artifact identity are preserved. - [ ] Root cause explains every material observation. - [ ] Mitigation is reversible and does not destroy forensic state. - [ ] Permanent fix has a regression test. - [ ] Recovery is confirmed through user-impact telemetry. Trigger Activate when a request changes PostgreSQL source, configuration, infrastructure, data contracts, or production behavior. Do not activate for a documentation-only mention with no technical decision. Why Model constraints in the database, inspect actual plans, keep transactions short, and make every migration backward compatible. The skill converts that principle into evidence gates that an agent cannot skip. Inputs - Repository rules and ownership boundaries. - Exact runtime/toolchain evidence from manifests or platform APIs. - Requested behavior and acceptance tests. - Sanitized logs, traces, metrics, plans, or screenshots when diagnosing. - Deployment topology, SLO, data classification, and rollback mechanism. How 1. Discover the nearest repository instructions and established implementation pattern. 2. State the invariant, trust boundary, failure mode, and rollback boundary. 3. Select the matching prompt under ../prompts/. 4. Make the smallest coherent change; preserve public contracts unless migration is approved. 5. Run native formatting, static analysis, unit/integration tests, security checks, and build/package validation. 6. Apply ../checklists/code-review.md. 7. For release work, apply ../checklists/deployment.md and capture evidence. Verification 1. Verify that constraints encode invariants. 2. Verify that EXPLAIN ANALYZE supports index decisions. 3. Verify that transactions are short and retry-aware. 4. Verify that migration has expand/contract and rollback controls. 5. Record commands, exit status, artifact identity, and links to retained evidence. Termination criteria Finish only when acceptance tests and both relevant checklists pass, or when a named blocker with owner and required evidence is recorded. docs.text: Python Production Skill Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Provide a deterministic procedure for generating, changing, diagnosing, or releasing a package, service endpoint, task, or library function with AI assistance. Trigger Activate when a request changes Python source, configuration, infrastructure, data contracts, or production behavior. Do not activate for a documentation-only mention with no technical decision. Why Use explicit types at boundaries, isolated environments, deterministic dependencies, and async only for genuinely asynchronous I/O. The skill converts that principle into evidence gates that an agent cannot skip. Inputs - Repository rules and ownership boundaries. - Exact runtime/toolchain evidence from manifests or platform APIs. - Requested behavior and acceptance tests. - Sanitized logs, traces, metrics, plans, or screenshots when diagnosing. - Deployment topology, SLO, data classification, and rollback mechanism. How 1. Discover the nearest repository instructions and established implementation pattern. 2. State the invariant, trust boundary, failure mode, and rollback boundary. 3. Select the matching prompt under ../prompts/. 4. Make the smallest coherent change; preserve public contracts unless migration is approved. 5. Run native formatting, static analysis, unit/integration tests, security checks, and build/package validation. 6. Apply ../checklists/code-review.md. 7. For release work, apply ../checklists/deployment.md and capture evidence. Verification 1. Verify that public boundaries are typed. 2. Verify that resources use context managers. 3. Verify that async code contains no blocking I/O. 4. Verify that dependencies are reproducible. 5. Record commands, exit status, artifact identity, and links to retained evidence. Unhappy path and recovery - If repository or version evidence is missing, stop and request it. - If a validator fails, fix the first causal error; never suppress the rule as the initial response. - If the failure cannot be reproduced, improve telemetry and preserve the incident state. - If a release gate fails, halt progression and execute the documented rollback or feature-disable path. - If credentials or regulated data appear in context, stop, revoke or rotate as required, and follow incident policy. Termination criteria Finish only when acceptance tests and both relevant checklists pass, or when a named blocker with owner and required evidence is recorded. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated package, service endpoint, task, or library function without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. docs.title: React Architecture Patterns
docs.description: Define the default production architecture for a React workload and the boundaries an AI-generated change must preserve.
docs.text: React Architecture Patterns Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Define the default production architecture for a React workload and the boundaries an AI-generated change must preserve. Why Keep rendering pure, derive values during render, and use Effects only to synchronize with external systems. A stable boundary reduces coupling, limits failure propagation, and makes ownership auditable. How Use Feature boundary with pure view: Route features expose a small public API; pure components render data while hooks own synchronization. Boundary rules 1. Validate identity, authorization, and input before domain mutation. 2. Keep dependency-specific types behind the infrastructure port. 3. Attach deadlines, cancellation, idempotency, and retry classification at the call boundary. 4. Emit traceable outcomes without secret or regulated payload leakage. 5. Version contracts and migrate producers before removing compatibility. Tradeoffs The extra adapter and contract code costs initial delivery time. It buys isolated tests, replaceable infrastructure, clearer ownership, and safer migrations. Anti-patterns - Split by technical file type across the application. This couples unrelated change rates and expands blast radius. - Do not hide remote calls, unbounded work, or mutable global state behind convenience helpers. - Do not introduce a distributed boundary without an owner, SLO, timeout, and failure policy. Enterprise considerations Assign owners to every boundary and data class. Enforce policy as code, retain architecture decisions and deployment evidence, and design regional, tenant, and regulatory isolation before data is written. Official guidance - React documentation - Rules of Hooks - WAI-ARIA APG Checklist - [ ] Domain and infrastructure boundaries are visible in code and telemetry. - [ ] Trust, data, transaction, and rollback boundaries are documented. - [ ] Dependency failure is bounded and tested. - [ ] Contract evolution is backward compatible. - [ ] Ownership and SLO are assigned. docs.title: React Common Error Workflow
docs.description: Diagnose recurring React failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error.
docs.text: React Common Error Workflow Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Diagnose recurring React failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error. Why Error text is a symptom, not a root cause. This workflow requires a discriminating observation before each repair. How 1. Preserve timestamps, correlation identifiers, artifact version, topology, and recent changes. 2. Stabilize user impact with the smallest reversible mitigation. 3. Capture the evidence named below before restarting or clearing state. 4. Test one ranked hypothesis at a time. 5. Add a regression test, alert, or policy after confirming root cause. Symptom Likely causal class Required repair Primary evidence --- --- --- --- Rendered more hooks than during the previous render A Hook is called conditionally or after an early return. Move every Hook to the component top level and branch inside the Hook or rendered output. eslint-plugin-react-hooks Too many re-renders Render synchronously calls a state setter. Move the update to an event or external-system Effect and prove its termination condition. React DevTools Profiler Maximum update depth exceeded An Effect updates a dependency that changes on every execution. Remove derived state or stabilize the true external dependency. React DevTools Profiler Hydration mismatch Server and client render different initial trees. Make initial output deterministic and defer browser-only data until after hydration. browser console Stale event or Effect value A closure captured obsolete props or state. Declare every reactive dependency or use a functional state update. eslint-plugin-react-hooks 1. Rendered more hooks than during the previous render Confirm: Capture eslint-plugin-react-hooks and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: A Hook is called conditionally or after an early return. Repair: Move every Hook to the component top level and branch inside the Hook or rendered output. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 2. Too many re-renders Confirm: Capture React DevTools Profiler and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Render synchronously calls a state setter. Repair: Move the update to an event or external-system Effect and prove its termination condition. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 3. Maximum update depth exceeded Confirm: Capture React DevTools Profiler and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: An Effect updates a dependency that changes on every execution. Repair: Remove derived state or stabilize the true external dependency. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 4. Hydration mismatch Confirm: Capture browser console and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Server and client render different initial trees. Repair: Make initial output deterministic and defer browser-only data until after hydration. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 5. Stale event or Effect value Confirm: Capture eslint-plugin-react-hooks and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: A closure captured obsolete props or state. Repair: Declare every reactive dependency or use a functional state update. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. docs.title: React Native Common Error Workflow
docs.description: Diagnose recurring React Native failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error.
docs.text: React Native Common Error Workflow Version: 1.0.0 Updated: 2026-07-16 Purpose Diagnose recurring React Native failures from evidence and restore service without destructive trial and error. Why Error text is a symptom, not a root cause. This workflow requires a discriminating observation before each repair. How 1. Preserve timestamps, correlation identifiers, artifact version, topology, and recent changes. 2. Stabilize user impact with the smallest reversible mitigation. 3. Capture the evidence named below before restarting or clearing state. 4. Test one ranked hypothesis at a time. 5. Add a regression test, alert, or policy after confirming root cause. Symptom Likely causal class Required repair Primary evidence --- --- --- --- Invariant Violation: native module cannot be null Native dependency is absent, unlinked, or unavailable in the current runtime. Verify platform installation and rebuild the native application. native build and module registry Application has not been registered Entry registration failed or an earlier module exception aborted startup. Find the first bundler/runtime error and verify the registered app key. Metro logs VirtualizedLists should never be nested A virtualized list is inside a same-axis ScrollView. Use one virtualized parent and model surrounding content as header/footer. React Native warning Unable to resolve module Metro resolution, alias, case, or dependency graph is inconsistent. Correct the canonical import and reset cache only after fixing configuration. Metro resolver output UI freezes during interaction JavaScript or native main thread performs excessive synchronous work. Profile both threads and defer, batch, or move the measured bottleneck. React Native performance monitor 1. Invariant Violation: native module cannot be null Confirm: Capture native build and module registry and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Native dependency is absent, unlinked, or unavailable in the current runtime. Repair: Verify platform installation and rebuild the native application. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 2. Application has not been registered Confirm: Capture Metro logs and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Entry registration failed or an earlier module exception aborted startup. Repair: Find the first bundler/runtime error and verify the registered app key. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 3. VirtualizedLists should never be nested Confirm: Capture React Native warning and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: A virtualized list is inside a same-axis ScrollView. Repair: Use one virtualized parent and model surrounding content as header/footer. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 4. Unable to resolve module Confirm: Capture Metro resolver output and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: Metro resolution, alias, case, or dependency graph is inconsistent. Repair: Correct the canonical import and reset cache only after fixing configuration. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. 5. UI freezes during interaction Confirm: Capture React Native performance monitor and correlate it to the failing request, resource, or deployment revision. Cause: JavaScript or native main thread performs excessive synchronous work. Repair: Profile both threads and defer, batch, or move the measured bottleneck. Verify: Reproduce the original operation, prove the error signal is absent, prove the intended result is present, and watch the relevant saturation/error metric for one complete operational window. Tradeoffs This standard favors explicit contracts and deterministic validation over rapid, implicit configuration. It adds review work up front but reduces production ambiguity and rollback time. Anti-patterns - Do not accept generated diagnostic or repair without executing the technology's native validators. - Do not suppress diagnostics without recording the violated invariant and compensating control. - Do not introduce a dependency when the platform already provides the required capability. Enterprise considerations Record artifact provenance, reviewer identity, test evidence, security findings, and deployment approval. Redact credentials and regulated data before sending context to an AI system. Enforce the same policy, audit, retention, and separation-of-duties controls used for human-authored changes. Official guidance - React Native documentation - Performance overview - Accessibility Checklist - [ ] Incident timeline and affected artifact identity are preserved. - [ ] Root cause explains every material observation. - [ ] Mitigation is reversible and does not destroy forensic state. - [ ] Permanent fix has a regression test. - [ ] Recovery is confirmed through user-impact telemetry.
